You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
`place` is drawn exactly as written in every image of the section that happens there, so it names only the physical place where most of the section happens: its land or water, buildings, their layout and fixed features, as they look throughout the section. Put no people, animals, crowds, events, time of day or weather in `place`.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. Describe only the shared place, weather and light. Where the section shows one of them, its presence may appear only as smoke, cloud, fire, wind or light spread through the place. Never describe its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train, face, hands, hair, body or silhouette, even as an empty seat, a denial or a figure made of light: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement. People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples. Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments. Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.

Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided. The children of Israel went into the middle of the sea on the dry ground; and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left. The Egyptians pursued, and went in after them into the middle of the sea: all of Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen. In the morning watch, Yahweh looked out on the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and confused the Egyptian army. He took off their chariot wheels, and they drove them heavily; so that the Egyptians said, “Let’s flee from the face of Israel, for Yahweh fights for them against the Egyptians!”

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action, inside the section place when one is given. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Moses

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.
- Only Moses, Red Sea have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

Action: The wind-driven waters pull back and divide, leaving dry seabed between two walls of water
Setting: The shoreline edge where the walled waters rise on either side of the exposed sand and rock floor
Secondary elements: Strong east wind streaming across the scene, a pillar of fire and cloud glowing overhead, the distant shore of the wilderness in view
Mood: Awe, quiet power and trembling expectancy
Time of day: Deep night giving way to the first grey light of dawn, strong wind all night
Composition: Wide view from the shore, Moses in the foreground facing the parting sea, the divided waters receding into the distance

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
- Image 2: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
